headline: Agents boom, offices empty, grids strain: a richer, angrier world taxes compute

events: Spring capability jump: agentic models reliably complete multi-day software, legal and accounting workflows; enterprise 'agent seats' priced below offshore labour
Indian and Philippine BPO hiring freezes; first mass layoffs in US/EU back-office, call-centre and junior-developer roles
Hyperscaler capex passes $700bn; US utilities file record interconnection requests and gas-turbine order books sell out to 2031
Fed cuts to 3.0% as services inflation eases; equity indices hit records led by a handful of AI and power firms
US-China agree a tariff truce extension; chips export controls stay but trade tensions plateau
Second capability jump: general-purpose agents plus cheap humanoid/warehouse robotics pilots spread into logistics and retail
Wholesale power prices spike 40-70% in PJM, Ireland, Netherlands and Japan; electricity-driven inflation pushes G20 average to 4.7%
Central banks split: Fed holds amid unemployment rising to 5.4%; ECB hikes once on energy, then reverses
US election fought over 'AI job theft' and power bills; winner promises a compute levy and worker transition accounts
Ukraine ceasefire along frozen lines holds uneasily; Gulf states pour sovereign wealth into data-centre campuses
AI-equity correction of ~30% as model prices collapse and margins compress; two leveraged data-centre REITs and a private-credit fund fail
Global unemployment peaks at 7.2%; graduate unemployment above 15% in UK, South Korea, Spain; youth protests in Lagos, Dhaka, Manila over vanished outsourcing jobs
US passes compute/automation levy (2% of AI service revenue) funding wage insurance; EU adopts AI Dividend pilot in five states
Pakistan, Egypt, Kenya and Sri Lanka enter debt restructurings as remittances and services exports fall
Taiwan Strait naval standoff over chip-fab inspections; resolved without blockade but insurance costs spike
Productivity growth in US hits 3.5% y/y; cheaper AI-run healthcare triage, tax filing and tutoring lower some living costs
Small modular reactor orders, geothermal and record solar+storage build ease power crunch; renewables reach 41% of electricity
Sahel-Coastal West Africa conflict escalates into a regional war involving Burkina Faso, Mali and Côte d'Ivoire militias
AI-assisted drug discovery yields first approved therapies designed end-to-end by models
France and Italy see populist governments elected on anti-automation, pro-pension platforms; bond spreads widen but ECB backstops
Unemployment eases to 6.3% as care, construction, energy and 'human-verified' service jobs absorb workers, often at lower pay
Top 1% wealth share in US reaches post-1929 high; corporate profits at record share of GDP
Global compute-tax coordination talks at G20 stall; three countries adopt partial basic-income schemes
AI agents run a majority of new corporate software and customer interactions; 61% of firms use AI in production
Emissions decline slightly despite data-centre demand as solar and storage outpace load growth

winners: Frontier AI labs, chipmakers and power-equipment/utility firms
Owners of capital and land near grid capacity (Gulf states, Nordics, Texas)
Skilled trades, nurses and energy workers in tight physical-labour markets
losers: Entry-level white-collar workers and recent graduates
Services-export economies dependent on BPO and remittances (Philippines, parts of India, Kenya)
Indebted frontier sovereigns and electricity-poor households facing higher bills
bullets: Global output is meaningfully larger, with US and China productivity booms, but gains accrue overwhelmingly to capital and a small pool of AI-complementary workers.
Routine office work has been hollowed out: ~185m jobs displaced cumulatively, re-absorbed only partly and often into lower-paid physical and care work.
Electricity is the new binding constraint and political flashpoint; data centres consume ~6% of global power and household bills are a top voter grievance.
Fiscal positions worsened via transition spending and wage insurance; compute levies exist in the US and parts of the EU but raise less than hoped.
Populist, anti-automation parties hold power or lead polls across much of Europe and Latin America; trust in institutions has fallen to new lows.
The services-led development path is broken for South Asia and Africa, feeding debt distress, migration pressure and youth unrest.
Trade tensions stayed contained, but chip and compute access became the main axis of US-China rivalry.
Clean energy build accelerated alongside gas, so warming tracks roughly on trend despite the power surge.
wildcard: In 2029 a widely deployed autonomous procurement agent triggered a cascading flash-crash in European power futures, halting trading for two days and prompting the first binding EU rules on agent-to-agent market activity.
image_description: A former paralegal in a hi-vis vest installs rooftop batteries in a Columbus suburb while her phone's AI agent negotiates her overdue power bill, past a shuttered office park repurposed as a humming data centre.
